summary: Intermittent EU->US egress port flapping causing streaming timeouts for AcmePay
description:
Issue summary: Customer AcmePay reports intermittent 504 / streaming disconnects and long p99 latencies for streaming generation in production. Problem appears as sudden timeouts for EU region customers where requests are routed to our US egress, and the stream is aborted after 30-90s.

Impact: Multiple production customers using AcmePay app see failed streaming responses and client reconnect churn. Estimated 12% failed streaming sessions for impacted tenant between 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC and 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC. Severity: customer-facing latency/timeouts, potential revenue impact.

Environment: prod, eu-west front-door -> anycast egress -> us-east serving nodes observed in traces. Customer pinned model: gptx-large-v1. Dedicated account routing? No (enterprise self-serve hosted).

Steps to reproduce (provided by Support and reproduced in-house):
1) Send a streaming generation request from eu-west region (~client IPs in Frankfurt).
2) Observe request headers and trace-id.
3) Note egress selection in request trace; occasionally the request is routed through us-east egress proxies.
4) Streaming connection stalls between 20s-90s and receives a 504 gateway timeout or TLS connection reset.

Observed behavior: intermittent cross-region egress selection to us-east coincides with increased TCP retransmits, out-of-order packets, and final stream abort. Traces show the source port mapping at NAT changing mid-stream for the same client IP (suggests ephemeral port churn). BGP and anycast healthchecks did not show large-scale regional outage.

Expected behavior: EU front-door traffic should remain on eu-west egress for locality; streaming sessions should not be torn down by intermediate NAT port reuse or egress path changes.

Attached logs/metrics: request traces (trace-ids included inline in investigation notes), tcpdump snippets showing port reuse, Cloud NAT metrics showing ephemeral port utilization spikes, edge proxy logs indicating 502/504.

Temporary mitigation: Applied region-hint header for AcmePay routing that forces eu-west egress for their account (route_hint=eu-west). Increased API gateway keep-alive on customer route to 120s. Customer notified of workaround.

Next steps: SRE/Networking to validate NAT port pool sizing and any transient NAT gateway failures. Serving/runtime to confirm that our anycast selection logic does not flip active path on mid-stream port changes. Engineering to implement a short-term sticky egress mapping when NAT ephemeral port churn is detected for active streaming sessions.
comments: Support - Aisha Patel - 2026-03-10: Received alert from customer at 22:18 UTC reporting streaming failures. Collected sample trace ids and asked for correlation ids. Escalated to SRE due to P1 customer impact.

SRE - Daniel Kim - 2026-03-10: Initial triage shows bursts of Cloud NAT ephemeral port exhaustion in eu-west at 22:05-22:30 UTC and again at 00:12-00:45 UTC. Packets show port reuse and NAT mapping refresh mid-session. Opening network investigation and contacting cloud provider support.

Engineering - Priya Shah - 2026-03-11: Observed anycast egress weight logic will consider source ip:port tuple; if port remaps then we appear to select fallback egress. Adding logic item to avoid egress flip for established streaming sessions when only ephemeral port changed.

Support - Tessa Nguyen - 2026-03-11: Applied route_hint workaround for AcmePay and increased keep-alive; customer reports sharp drop in failures to ~1% (non-zero). Requesting SRE confirm root cause and a durable fix.

Networking - Marco Ruiz - 2026-03-12: Cloud provider confirmed transient NAT port allocation issue on their side; they increased port pool for our project and recommend adding NAT logging to correlate future events. We will also implement server-side sticky egress to tolerate port churn.
investigation_notes: 22:05 UTC spike: Cloud NAT ephemeral port utilization reached 98% for project n-777 in eu-west, per provider metrics.

TCP captures show same client IP initiating stream from port 51120 then provider NAT translated to ephemeral 62034; later mapping changed to 62078 mid-stream and our anycast selection used the new tuple, routing to us-east.
Anycast health checks remained green; no BGP flaps found. This rules out pure network path outage and points to NAT mapping churn as the proximate cause.
Hypothesis: NAT port exhaustion -> ephemeral port reuse -> source tuple change -> egress selection logic perceives new flow and routes to alternate egress -> streaming state mismatch -> timeout/504.
Risk: Without sticky egress, other customers sharing NAT may experience similar disruptions during provider maintenance or load spikes.
resolution:
In progress. Short-term: Applied route_hint and increased keep-alive for AcmePay; provider increased NAT port pool and acknowledged transient issue. Medium-term: engineering will implement sticky egress selection for active streaming sessions to avoid mid-stream egress flips (tracked in GH PR). Long-term: add NAT port utilization alerting and expand multi-region egress hysteresis logic.

Linked fixes: PR 2145 implements sticky egress support for the streaming session manager. Post-deploy, run soak tests for 48h and monitor p99 of streaming sessions for AcmePay.

Follow-up actions:
- ENG-2145 (serving-runtime): sticky egress implementation (owner: Priya Shah)
- NET-330 (networking ops): enable NAT port utilization alerting and request permanent port pool increase (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- CS-022 (customer success): confirm with AcmePay after deployment and schedule a technical review call.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 23:05 UTC - Tessa Nguyen (Support): Notified AcmePay workspace that we identified transient NAT port pressure in eu-west as likely cause. Provided temporary route_hint workaround and ETA for next update.

2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Marco Ruiz (Networking): Follow-up to AcmePay: cloud provider increased NAT capacity; we are implementing a platform-side sticky egress change. Asked customer to report any further anomalies.
